methods.original_objective: Original ACI adapts a prediction-set miscoverage level under sequential feedback. B4 is a sparse-feedback dual-threshold adaptation.
required_observations_and_supervision: Common current score; selectively queried labels; current-memory normal and defect anchor scores.
methods.update_equations_and_state: Original: one alpha state and realized error each step. B4: on queried y=0, aN += gammaN*(alpha-1[pred=defect]); on queried y=1, aD += gammaD*(beta-1[pred=normal]); missing side is not zero risk; empirical anchors set exact count bounds.
methods.initialization_and_warmup: B4 alpha=beta=0.10; gamma_N=gamma_D=0.005; class side moves only on queried feedback; current-memory anchor bounds.
methods.distributional_assumptions: ACI paper theorem concerns sequential prediction-set coverage under its update/feedback setup. Sparse selectively queried labels, classwise physical defect metrics, serial dependence and dynamic memory are outside this implementation mapping.
methods.supported_prediction_output: Repository controller returns binary defect/normal decisions; original ACI is a set-valued prediction method.
adaptations: Original ACI uses a per-time realized miscoverage/error update alpha_(t+1)=alpha_t+gamma*(alpha-err_t) after observing each outcome and targets long-run prediction-set coverage.
Repository B4 uses separate normal/defect sides and updates only when a queried label is disclosed.
B4 applies class-conditional anchor threshold bounds for physical defect FPR/FNR; it is not the original ACI objective or update law.
required_online_inputs: Common current score; selectively queried labels; current-memory normal and defect anchor scores.
known_limitations: No original ACI feedback at every step.
No original single-alpha recursion.
No ACI finite-time/anytime guarantee transfers.
Not source-equivalent despite literature inspiration.

methods.original_objective: POT/GPD tail threshold for rare high score alarms at registered risk q=0.001.
required_observations_and_supervision: Every past and current causal unlabeled scalar score; no physical labels or query feedback.
methods.update_equations_and_state: At high empirical u, fit GPD to strict exceedances with Grimshaw MLE; threshold zq = u + (sigma/xi)*((q*n/Nu)^(-xi)-1), with exponential limit at xi=0; an alarm is score > zq and excluded from count/peak updates.
methods.initialization_and_warmup: n_init=1000; initial level=0.98; q=0.001; Grimshaw starts=10; root tolerance=1e-6. Predictions are explicitly unavailable during initialization.
methods.distributional_assumptions: The paper’s univariate stream/POT tail conditions require a sufficiently high threshold and stable tail behavior; memory-dependent scores can be serially dependent and nonstationary.
methods.supported_prediction_output: Binary alarm after warm-up; no prediction during startup.
adaptations: Python implementation follows Siffer et al. paper equations and has independent equation/state tests; no compiled author-C trace parity.
Input is a changing-memory image-level scalar score, not the paper’s assumed stationary/IID stream setting.
Uses a strict score > threshold alarm rule; common controller thresholds may use >=, so exact ties can differ.
Initial empirical 98th percentile uses NumPy linear interpolation, a convention not specified by the paper.
Grimshaw root recovery includes deterministic sign-bracket roots in addition to the paper-style multistart bounded optimization.

methods.original_objective: Remove local mean/trend from the score stream, then apply POT to the residual stream.
required_observations_and_supervision: Every past and current causal unlabeled scalar score; no physical labels or query feedback.
methods.update_equations_and_state: r_t = x_t - mean(last d accepted normal raw observations); run SPOT on r_t; reconstruct threshold as mean(window)+zq. Alarms update neither POT nor the moving mean window.
methods.initialization_and_warmup: d=50 raw-score window, then 1000 residual initialization observations; level=0.98; q=0.001; predictions unavailable through 1050 startup observations.
methods.distributional_assumptions: Stationarity of detrended residuals is required by the paper formulation; memory-dependent drift may persist after local-mean removal.
methods.supported_prediction_output: Binary alarm after warm-up; no prediction during the first 1050 observations.
adaptations: Python implementation follows Siffer et al. paper equations and has independent equation/state tests; no compiled author-C trace parity.

methods.original_objective: Confidence sequence for a score-stream p-quantile, with change detection; output is benign/anomaly/abstain relative to confidence bounds, not a physical image-defect label.
required_observations_and_supervision: Full causal scalar score history; no physical defect labels, query feedback, or C64 matching.
methods.update_equations_and_state: Algorithm 1: score above upper bound => anomaly, below lower bound => benign, otherwise abstain. Algorithm 2 checks forward/backward confidence-set intersections. Algorithm 3 abstains/resets on detected change. Empty prefix is ABSTAIN_COLD_START.
methods.initialization_and_warmup: Primary p=0.99, delta=0.01; clipped q=0 endpoint -infinity, q=1 endpoint +infinity; separate empirical-extrema sensitivity policy.
methods.distributional_assumptions: Paper assumptions concern IID or piecewise-stationary scalar score segments, continuity/no atoms and change-point spacing. Dynamic-memory scores and physical defects are different target/assumption regimes.
adaptations: Paper Algorithms 1–3 and Eqs. (1)–(2) are implemented with explicit endpoint/cold-start conventions and independent reference-trace tests.
No verified author code was located and no author trace parity is claimed.
Stage 1-A did not include B6 in the physical defect binary leaderboard.
required_online_inputs: Full causal scalar score history; no physical defect labels, query feedback, or C64 matching.
known_limitations: At p=.99, delta=.01, the primary upper endpoint remains clipped to 1 through n=353017; at Real-IAD stream lengths near 3815 it cannot label a score as anomaly under this endpoint policy.
Confidence-sequence quantile labels are not physical defect labels.
No legitimate full binary BA/FPR/FNR ranking against this B6 implementation.
Implementation complexity is O(T^2 log T) worst-case cumulative Algorithm 3 without resets and O(T log T) peak auxiliary space; no method runtime/memory benchmark in Stage 1-A.
